name: capture-status
about: A live game capture (agent-browser / Playwright screenshot, progress or timelapse frame): is it a usable frame of the 3D world, or did the capture catch a loading screen, a title card, a menu, a blank frame or an error? D3 (2026-10-03, project/archive/2026-10-03-decision-models.md): 376 hand-labelled real frames, 'not the world' AUC 0.998, 99 % of bad frames flagged at 3 % of good ones flagged. The 'corrupt' answer is logged but does not flag: it caught 1 of 4 real render glitches (AUC 0.88).
state: A screenshot taken by an automated test of Wildshard, a first-person 3D web game, at phone or desktop size. A good frame shows the 3D game world (terrain, sky, water, buildings, plants, creatures), usually with HUD buttons, a minimap and small labels drawn on top.

screen.instructions: What does this screenshot mostly show?

criteria.world: The 3D game world (terrain, sky, buildings, plants, characters), with or without HUD buttons and labels on top
criteria.loading: A loading screen, splash or title card, a progress bar, or the game still starting up
criteria.blank: An empty frame: all black, all white or one flat colour, with no scene
criteria.menu: A menu, settings panel, pause screen, full-screen map or dialog covering most of the screen
criteria.error: An error message, crash report or browser error page

corrupt.instructions: Do solid black squares or rectangles, or blocks of garbage pixels, break up the 3D scene? A rendering glitch, not a shadow, a dark object or a UI panel.

calibrated.note: v1 flagged loading/blank/error only (recall 78 % at 0.5): the phone title cards read as 'menu'. v2's flag counts menu too; it was chosen after seeing v1's results, so its numbers are not yet confirmed on fresh frames.
